title: Space has a price: the holes and the freeing break
outcomes: Finds the holes that advanced pawns leave behind
Checks whether the lever that would free the cramped side is ready, by looking at the pawn that supports it
Tells a position where the space edge is safe from one where pushing further costs something
Recognises a position with no space edge and no freeing break to worry about

steps.text: In **Space: count the safe squares, then look for the lever** you counted space. Now ask what space costs. Pawns pushed far leave **holes** behind them: squares none of that side's pawns can attack, now or by advancing. The cramped side asks one question: is my freeing lever ready? Rule of thumb: before a lever, check that the pawn it attacks cannot simply punish the push, and that you can recapture on the square it lands on.

steps.caption: Black to move. White's pawns on c4, d4 and e5 take a lot of space, and the f-pawn is gone. The lever ...f6 attacks the head e5. The engine still prefers White, but ...f6 is the cramped side's best way to cut the edge.

line.say: The lever attacks e5, the pawn that holds the space.
White takes the pawn on f6.
The bishop recaptures. The space pawn on e5 is gone and Black has room.

steps.text: **Rule of thumb, with conditions.** A space edge leaves holes, and the cramped side can hit it with a lever. Here White stays better after the lever; it only reduces the edge. A lever is ready when the push runs into no tactic and you can recapture on the lever square (here the queen can, once the e-pawn has left e7). In the second position the e-pawn stands on e7 and ...f6 is rated clearly worse; we know the difference, not the full reason.

steps.title: Same space, the same lever
steps.prompt: Predict for each position whether ...f6 is a reasonable move. In the second, one Black pawn is on another square; in the third, one White piece is.

Look back at the contrast positions. In which one did you misjudge ...f6 first? Name the pawn or piece whose square changed the answer, then rate how sure you were (low, medium, high) before you saw the result.
